evidence: backend/servers/api-server/src/services/accounting.rs:49-107 — process_statement_upload() creates the parent bank_statement row first (create_bank_statement_rls, L61-71) and then parses + inserts CSV lines one at a time inside the `for result in rdr.deserialize()` loop (L73-100). Both a CSV deserialize/parse failure (L74-81: `AppError::BadRequest`) and a per-line insert failure (L96-99) return `?` mid-loop, so execution aborts after the statement and a partial subset of lines have already been written.

backend/servers/api-server/src/routes/accounting/statements.rs:49-54 — the handler calls process_statement_upload(&mut rls, ...) passing the RLS-scoped connection guard, NOT a transaction. Each repository insert therefore commits independently (connection auto-commit), so there is no rollback on the mid-loop error path: the orphaned parent statement plus any lines inserted before the bad row remain committed in the DB while the user receives a 4xx/5xx and believes the upload failed.

Impact: data-integrity / financial-ledger pollution. A statement export whose Nth row has a malformed date (L77-81 accepts only %Y-%m-%d or %d.%m.%Y) or amount persists a partial statement with rows 1..N-1 and silently triggers run_payment_matcher on the partial set (L103). On retry the user re-uploads, producing a duplicate statement. Landable backend-only fix: wrap the create-statement + line-insert loop (+ optionally the matcher) in a single sqlx transaction (begin on the RLS connection, commit only after the loop) so a parse/insert failure rolls the whole upload back. Reachability traced end-to-end (POST statement-upload route -> service -> repo); kept at medium because confirmation of the orphan requires observing commit behaviour at runtime, which static analysis cannot execute.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/accounting.rs:197-203 — the payment matcher's amount-corroboration step compares `line.amount == remaining_amount` (and the `<=` partial-payment branch) purely on the rust_decimal::Decimal numeric value. The bank statement line carries `currency: String` (set from the CSV at accounting.rs:89) and the Invoice carries `currency: String` (backend/crates/db/src/models/accounting.rs:76-93), but run_payment_matcher (accounting.rs:110-226) never compares the two currencies anywhere while scoring.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/accounting.rs:182-225 — confidence is accumulated across variable-symbol (0.8), amount (0.15 exact / 0.05 partial) and IBAN (0.05) signals, then compared against threshold 0.5 (L155). Because currency is ignored, a line amounting to e.g. EUR 1000 numerically equals a CZK 1000 remaining balance and receives the +0.15 exact-amount corroboration; if the two also share a variable symbol the pair auto-suggests a cross-currency PaymentMatch (L223-239), and the amount tie-breaker can even promote a wrong-currency invoice above the correct-currency one.

Impact: incorrect payment-to-invoice reconciliation across currencies on a multi-currency ledger (CZK/EUR are both first-class here — see the CZ/SK IBAN handling at accounting.rs:17-26 and the CZ date format support). Landable backend-only fix: gate the amount-corroboration branches (and ideally the whole candidate) on `line.currency.eq_ignore_ascii_case(&invoice.currency)` so amounts are only ever compared within the same currency. Call path traced (process_statement_upload -> run_payment_matcher, also invokable directly); medium confidence because the real-world blast radius depends on tenants actually holding mixed-currency open invoices with shared variable symbols.
